plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above broad blue-green leaves. Thousands of cultivars exist in nearly every color and in forms ranging from single to fringed and parrot types. In many temperate regions, late April is the peak of the tulip display.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to early May in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Netherlands, northern Europe, North America, and temperate gardens worldwide; native to Central Asia
plants.funFact: During the 17th-century Dutch 'Tulip Mania', single bulbs sold for more than the price of a house in Amsterdam.

plants.name: Cornus florida
plants.description: A small deciduous understory tree whose showy 'flowers' are actually four large petal-like bracts surrounding a cluster of tiny true flowers. It lights up woodland edges in the eastern United States in late April, and it turns brilliant red in autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late spring (April to May)
plants.location: Eastern United States and northeastern Mexico; widely planted in gardens
plants.funFact: The showy white parts are modified leaves called bracts; the real flowers are the small greenish-yellow cluster at the center.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing tree with fern-like foliage and large panicles of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere it is mostly a spring bloomer (Oct-Nov), but in tropical and equatorial highlands such as parts of Central America and the Caribbean, as well as in parts of Northern Hemisphere subtropics, it can produce flowers in spring months including April and May.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (April to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; planted in Mexico, Florida, California, South Africa, Australia, and elsewhere
plants.funFact: Fallen jacaranda blossoms create purple carpets on streets, and in South Africa Pretoria is known as the 'Jacaranda City'.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A large, dramatic shrub with a flower head up to 30 cm across, composed of colorful bracts surrounding a central cone of tiny flowers. It is adapted to fire-prone fynbos and has leathery leaves that resist drought. Flowering peaks in southern autumn and spring, with scattered blooms through autumn months such as April.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly late summer to spring in South Africa, with autumn blooms in April to May
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape regions of South Africa (fynbos); cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its genus name comes from the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape, a nod to the many forms of proteas.
